_note: Set B, VERSIONED WITH THE RULES (12 files: top p1..p8, bottom p1..p4). tableVersion 1224-1 — the planner at 93ae32bf8 (planner v3 A1 #1217 + A1b #1224 + A3 #1219): the pocket's passes take the cutter's own row step-over, and the leftover tolerance never forgives tall material. Bottom gains the ⌀0.9 flat's own program (3→4); top keeps 8 with the pocket and curved-rough programs changed. The e2e reads this table as the cross-door check.
rule: (a) A CANDIDATE CHAIN IS RANKED BY THE TIME IT WILL REALLY TAKE (#1186 rule 1), ties to fewer bit changes then owned; (b) EVERY FLAT MAY PROPOSE AS A PRIMARY, shortlisted to the incumbent and the best own-row flat (#1192), and a cutter that can FREE the profile always joins when none shortlisted can (#1195); (c) THE FREEING CONTOUR IS A HARD CONSTRAINT (#1195, the analyst’s field): no chain is a candidate without a cutter whose STATED flute reaches the profile’s actual posted depth; the pick refuses only when nothing owned reaches or the operator pinned a cutter that does not, with a named sentence; (d) ONE CUTTER PER SHAPE AND DIAMETER, only on a job with a setup boundary (#1186 rule 6, gated by the setup count). (e) planner v3 A1/A1b: a leftover tolerance between chains within 0.5 % of the surface, applied only between chains leaving the same number of TALL cells (standing >1 mm above the goal) (#1217, #1224); (f) planner v3 A3: a pocket's step-over is the cutter's own feed row's step-over, capped at its radius (#1219).
source: casemaker cut <job>.cutjob.json --location ~/setb-inputs/location.json --catalogue ~/setb-inputs/catalogue.json, branch 1219-pocket-stepover @ 93ae32bf8 (A1 #1217 + A1b #1224 + A3 #1219), dave-1, 2026-11-11
